reasoning: The 1890 Isidore Liseux Paris edition is a well-documented English translation from Latin (confirmed WorldCat, Stanford, multiple dealers), covering 6 of 7 dialogues. A c.1930 'Parisien Society' edition claims to add the 7th dialogue (first complete English). Reynolds 2024 on Archive.org disputes this, calling his translation 'the first known English translation of Fescennini.' Either way, prior English translations from Latin are firmly established from 1890 onward — not_first is clear.
